back: The legal right to possess, use and control a resource and decide who else may use it.
The ability to use a resource or benefit from it, whether or not one owns it.
Policies that increase the share of the economy owned and controlled by indigenous Zimbabweans.

front: What does CAMPFIRE stand for and when did it begin?
back: Communal Areas Management Programme for Indigenous Resources; 1989.

front: What did the Indigenisation and Economic Empowerment Act (2007) require?
back: Most larger businesses to be at least 51 per cent owned by indigenous Zimbabweans (later narrowed by amendments).

front: What did the Water Act of 1998 change?
back: It ended private ownership of water; water is held by the state and allocated by permit.

front: How was wildlife controlled in the colonial era?
back: Game laws made hunting by Africans illegal in most cases; parks were run by the colonial state.
When a small, well-connected group takes most of the benefits meant for many people.

front: Give two benefits and two problems of efforts to widen access since 1980.
back: Benefits: wider indigenous ownership; community income (CAMPFIRE). Problems: elite capture and corruption; human-wildlife conflict or reduced investment.
